dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُحَمَّدٍ) An Arabic name, on the pattern mufaʿʿal from al-ḥamd (praise); the doubling in it is for frequency, as you say "I honoured him (karramtuhu), so he is mukarram" and "I glorified him, so he is muʿaẓẓam" when you have done that time after time. It is transferred from the adjective, by way of good omen that his praise would be abundant — and so he was ﷺ. Some transmitters of knowledge narrated, in what Ibn Durayd related, that when the Prophet ﷺ was born, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ordered a camel to be slaughtered, and it was slaughtered, and he invited the men of Quraysh. It was their custom with a newborn, if he was born at the onset of night, to turn a cooking pot over him until morning. They did that with the Prophet ﷺ, and in the morning the pot had split open from over him and he was gazing up at the sky. When the men of Quraysh came and had eaten, they said to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: "What have you named this son of yours?"
He said: "I have named him Muḥammad." They said: "This is not one of the names of your forefathers." He said: "I wanted him to be praised in the heavens and the earth." One says: a man maḥmūd (praised) and muḥammad. Al-Aʿshā said:
إليك أبيت اللعن كان كلالها ... إلى الواحد الفرد الجواد المحمّد
(To you — may you be spared the curse — was her weariness [spent], to the one, the unique, the generous, the much-praised.)
So maḥmūd does not indicate abundance, while muḥammad indicates it; and what indicates the difference between them is the poet's saying:
فلست بمحمود ولا بمحمد ... ولكنما أنت الحبط الحباتر
(You are neither praised nor much-praised; you are only the bloated, stunted one.)
The Arabs in the Jāhiliyya named some of their sons with it, among them: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān al-Juʿfī, the poet, who lived in the time of Imruʾ al-Qays and whom he called "Shuwayʿir" (the little poet); Muḥammad ibn Khawlī al-Hamdānī; Muḥammad ibn Bilāl ibn Uḥayḥa, who was the husband of Salmā bint ʿAmr, the grandmother of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, mother of his grandfather; Muḥammad ibn Sufyān ibn Mujāshiʿ ibn Dārim; Muḥammad ibn Maslama al-Anṣārī; and Abū Muḥammad ibn Aws ibn Zayd, who was present at Badr.
(بالَهُمْ) Al-bāl: the heart — one says "the matter did not occur to my mind (bi-bālī)"; state and living — one says "so-and-so is of easy bāl"; the mind — one says "so-and-so is of downcast bāl"; and what one is concerned with — one says "this is not of my bāl", i.e. of what I care about; "a matter of bāl", i.e. one that is attended to; and "mā bāluka", i.e. what is your affair? Al-Jawharī said: «Al-bāl is also the ease of living; one says "so-and-so is rakhiyy al-bāl", i.e. of easy living.» The wording of al-Bayḍāwī: «(وأصلح بالهم), i.e. their state in religion and in this world, through granting success and support.» The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «Al-bāl is thought; you say "such-and-such occurred in my bāl". It is not put into the dual or plural, and their saying bālāt as its plural is anomalous.» The wording of al-Qāmūs: «Al-bāl: state, mind, heart, and the great whale; and with tāʾ marbūṭa [bāla]: the flask, the leather bag, and the perfume container.»
(أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ) You have inflicted much slaughter on them. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Athkhana fī al-arḍ ithkhānan: he marched against the enemy and slaughtered them widely; and athkhantuhu: I weakened him with wounds and enfeebled him.»
(الْوَثاقَ) With fatḥa and kasra: the name of that by which something is bound. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-wathāq is the fetter, the rope and the like, with fatḥa or kasra on the wāw; the plural is wuthuq, like ribāṭ / rubuṭ and ʿanāq / ʿunuq.»
(أَوْزارَها) Its implements and burdens without which it cannot stand, such as weapons and horses. Al-Aʿshā said:
وأعددت للحرب أوزارها ... رماحا طوالا وخيلا ذكورا
(And I prepared for war its burdens: long spears and stallion horses.)
The wording of al-Kashshāf: «They were called its awzār because, since it cannot do without dragging them, it is as though it carries them and bears them; and when it ends, it is as though it has laid them down. It was also said that its awzār are its sins, meaning: until the people of war, who are the polytheists, abandon their polytheism and their sins by embracing Islam.»

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (صدّوا) is conjoined to (كفروا); (عن سبيل الله) are attached to (صدّوا). (أضلّ أعمالهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring to Allah the Exalted, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of (الذين). Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted (الذين) to be accusative by a verb indicated by what is mentioned, i.e. "He led astray those who disbelieved". (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَآمَنُوا بِما نُزِّلَ عَلى مُحَمَّدٍ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا), and (آمنوا بما نزل على محمد) is also conjoined. The wāw is parenthetical; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الحق) its khabar; and (من ربهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بالَهُمْ) The clause (كفّر عنهم) is the khabar of (الذين آمنوا); (سيئاتهم) is a direct object; and (أصلح بالهم) is conjoined to (كفّر عنهم سيئاتهم). (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْباطِلَ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأن الذين كفروا) its khabar; and the clause (اتبعوا الباطل) is the khabar of (أن). (وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) Conjoined to what preceded; its i'rab has been given. (كَذلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثالَهُمْ) (كذلك) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. like that striking [of examples] Allah strikes for people their examples. The meaning of striking the example here will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَإِذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَضَرْبَ الرِّقابِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the command within its domain consequent on what precedes it. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; what governs it is an implied verb, which is also what governs (ضرب الرقاب), its implied form being "then strike the necks at the time of your meeting the enemy"; the maṣdar itself does not govern it because it is emphatic. The clause (لقيتم) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (الذين) is the object of (لقيتم), and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila. The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; (ضرب) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and (الرقاب) is muḍāf ilayhi. (حَتَّى إِذا أَثْخَنْتُمُوهُمْ فَشُدُّوا الْوَثاقَ فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِداءً) (حتى) is a particle of inception, i.e. clauses begin after it; Abū Ḥayyān made it a particle of limit and of the genitive, saying: «And this is a limit for the striking.» (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (أثخنتموهم) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذا); (شدّوا الوثاق) is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object. The fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); (إما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (منّا) and (فداء) are two maṣdars made accusative by a verb that may not be made overt, because when a maṣdar is brought to detail the outcome of a clause, it must be accusative by an implied verb; the implied form is "either you show favour (tamunnū) as a favour, or you ransom (tufādū) as a ransom". Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted them to be two direct objects of an implied governing word, its implied form being "grant them a favour and accept from them a ransom" — and that is not the right view. (بعد) is an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. after capturing them and tightening their bonds. (حَتَّى تَضَعَ الْحَرْبُ أَوْزارَها) (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; together with what it governs it is attached either to the striking and the binding, or to the favour and the ransom, because it is a limit for all of that, according to a detailed discussion you will find set out at length in the books of the jurists — this is not its place. More explanation will come in the section on Rhetoric. (تضع) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after (حتى); (الحرب) is the agent and (أوزارها) a direct object. (ذلِكَ وَلَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَانْتَصَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَا بَعْضَكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ) (ذلك) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the matter concerning them is what has been mentioned of killing and capture and what follows of favour and ransom; you may also make it accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "do that". The wāw is resumptive; (لو) is conditional; (يشاء الله) is an imperfect verb and its agent; the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو); (انتصر) is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "He", i.e. Allah the Exalted. (ولكن): the wāw is a conjunction or of ḥāl, and (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened. The lām is causal; (يبلو) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the lām and what it governs are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He commanded you to fight"; (بعضكم) is a direct object, and (ببعض) are attached to (يبلو). (وَالَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَلَنْ يُضِلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (قتلوا) is the ṣila; (في سبيل الله) are attached to (قتلوا). The fāʾ is linking, because of the sense of condition in the relative noun; (لن) is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; (يضل) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن), its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (أعمالهم) is a direct object; and the clause is the khabar of (الذين). (سَيَهْدِيهِمْ وَيُصْلِحُ بالَهُمْ) The sīn is a particle of the future; (يهديهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (يصلح) is conjoined to (يهدي), and (بالهم) is a direct object. (وَيُدْخِلُهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ عَرَّفَها لَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (يدخلهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (الجنة) is a second direct
object, by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and the clause (عرفها لهم) is resumptive or circumstantial. The meaning of (عرفها لهم) will come in the section on Benefits.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words, Exalted is He, «وأضلّ أعمالهم» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): He likened their deeds to stray camels that are left to perish, with no owner to guard them and look after them; or to water that gets lost in milk. The meaning is that the good deeds of the disbelievers were lost amid the whole of their evil deeds of disbelief and sins, until their good became consumed in the flood of their evil. Its counterpart for the believers is Allah's covering of their evil deeds within the shelter of their good deeds of faith and obedience, until their evil became expiated and effaced beside the good of their deeds. To this beautiful illustration of not accepting the good of the disbelievers and of overlooking the evil deeds of the believers the allusion was made in His words, Exalted is He, «كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم». The detail of that is that striking an example is the use of a current saying whose occasion of application is likened to its original occasion. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: where is the striking of examples? I say: in His making the following of falsehood an example for the deeds of the disbelievers and the following of truth an example for the deeds of the believers; or in making the leading astray an example for the failure of the disbelievers, and the expiation of evil deeds an example for the triumph of the believers.»
2- The synecdochic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in His words, Exalted is He, «فإذا لقيتم الذين كفروا فضرب الرقاب» there is a majāz mursal whose relation is mentioning the part and meaning the whole, because striking the necks is an expression for killing; but since a person is most often killed by striking his neck, it came to be an expression for killing. The trope was preferred for the depiction and embodiment it contains, because in this expression — as al-Zamakhsharī says — there is a harshness and severity not found in the word "killing", since it depicts killing in its most hideous form, namely cutting the neck and sending flying the member which is the head of the body, its highest part and the most prominent of its members.
3- In His words, Exalted is He, «حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها» there is an implicit or explicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya or taṣrīḥiyya). On the first, war is likened to riding-beasts bearing awzār, i.e. heavy loads; on the second, awzār is borrowed for the implements of war. There is also in it a trope in attribution (majāz fī al-isnād), for the laying down of burdens is attributed to the war, whereas it belongs only to its people.

* Benefits:
The meaning of His words, Exalted is He, «عرّفها لهم» is either from taʿrīf in the sense of delimiting, such that each one has a Garden set apart — and in al-Bukhārī there is what indicates the soundness of this view, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The believers will be delivered from the Fire, then they will be held on a bridge between the Garden and the Fire, until, when they have been refined and purified, they will be permitted to enter the Garden. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, each of them will be better guided to his dwelling in the Garden than to his dwelling that he had in this world»; or it is from al-ʿarf, which is fragrance. Ibn ʿAbbās said: He perfumed it for them with kinds of delights; and "a muʿarraf food", i.e. a seasoned one. The Arabs say: "ʿarraftu al-qidr" when you have seasoned the pot with salt and spices. And in the speech of one of them: "ʿazfun ka-nawḥ al-qamārī wa-ʿarfun ka-fawḥ al-qamārī" (a melody like the cooing of the turtle-doves, and a fragrance like the diffusing of the qamārī [aloes]); the first qamārī is the plural of qumrī, the name of a bird, and the second qamārī is an aloeswood attributed to a place in the land of India. So it is in al-Ṣiḥāḥ.

dervis-irab:7-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَتَعْساً) Al-taʿs: perishing and the frustration of hope. In al-Mukhtār: «Al-taʿs is perishing; its origin is falling on one's face (al-kabb), and it is the opposite of recovering (al-intiʿāsh). Taʿasa, of the pattern qaṭaʿa, and Allah made him perish (atʿasahu); and one says "taʿsan li-fulān", i.e. may Allah make perishing binding on him.» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Taʿisa taʿasan, of the pattern taʿiba, is a dialectal form, so he is taʿis like taʿib; it is made transitive by the vowel and by the hamza, so one says "Allah taʿasahu" with fatḥa, and "atʿasahu". In supplication: "taʿsan lahu", and "taʿisa wa-ntakasa" (may he fall and relapse): al-taʿs is that he falls on his face, and al-naks is that he does not get up after his fall until he falls a second time, which is worse than the first.» In al-Asās: «Taʿasa fulān, with fatḥa — kasra is not eloquent — and "taʿsan lahu", and Allah taʿasahu and atʿasahu. He said:
غداة هزمنا جمعهم بمقالع ... فآبوا بأتعاس على شر طائر
(The morning we routed their host with slings, so they returned in ruin under the worst of omens.)
And you say: "may Allah lower his cheek and ruin his fortune"; he is manḥūs mutʿūs (ill-starred and ruined); and this matter is a cause of ruin and ill-luck (mataʿsa manḥasa).» The wording of al-Qurṭubī: «There are ten views on al-taʿs. The first: remoteness, said by Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jurayj. The second: disgrace to them, said by al-Suddī. The third: wretchedness to them, said by Ibn Zayd. The fourth: a reviling of them from Allah, said by al-Ḥasan. The fifth: perishing to them, said by Thaʿlab. The sixth: frustration to them, said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Ziyād. The seventh: ugliness to them, related by al-Naqqāsh. The eighth: humiliation to them, also said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk. The ninth: evil to them, also said by Thaʿlab. The tenth: misery to them, said by Abū al-ʿĀliya.»

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَنْصُرُوا اللَّهَ يَنْصُرْكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَكُمْ) (يا أيها الذين آمنوا): its i'rab has been given many times. (إن) is conditional; (تنصروا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الله) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ينصركم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and (يثبت أقدامكم) is conjoined to the apodosis. A muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "the religion of Allah and His Messenger". (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَتَعْساً لَهُمْ وَأَضَلَّ أَعْمالَهُمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "they were ruined (taʿisū)", and it is what governs (تعسا); it may also be accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows it. The clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the fāʾ is linking, by likening the relative noun to a condition; (تعسا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, as above; (لهم) are attached to (تعسا), or are an adjective of it; and (أضل أعمالهم) is conjoined to the verb that made (تعسا) accusative. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَرِهُوا ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأنهم) its khabar; (أن) and its noun, and the clause (كرهوا) is its khabar; (ما) is a direct object, and the clause (أنزل الله) is the ṣila. (فأحبط) is conjoined to (كرهوا), and (أعمالهم) is a direct object. (أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (يسيروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (في الأرض) are attached to (يسيروا). (فينظروا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), and (ينظروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar of (كان); (عاقبة) is its postponed noun; (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi; and (من قبلهم) are attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. (دَمَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلِلْكافِرِينَ أَمْثالُها) The clause explains (كيف) and has no grammatical position. (دمر الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (عليهم) are attached to (دمر); and the object of (دمر) is omitted, its implied form being "He destroyed their selves, their wealth and what they had built"; you may also make (دمر) carry the meaning of "was wrathful", so that it needs no object. (للكافرين) is a fronted khabar and (أمثالها) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the pronoun refers back to the aforementioned outcome, i.e. the likes of the outcome of those before them; it may also refer to the destruction understood from His words (دمر الله عليهم), but the first is preferable. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَأَنَّ الْكافِرِينَ لا مَوْلى لَهُمْ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بأن) its khabar; (الله) is the noun of (أن), and (مولى الذين آمنوا) is the khabar of (أن). (وأن الكافرين) is conjoined to what preceded; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (مولى) is its noun and (لهم) its khabar; and the clause is the khabar of (أن). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) The clause explains His guardianship, Exalted is He, and what follows from it. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يدخل الذين آمنوا) is its khabar; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila and falls within its domain; (جنات) is a second direct object, by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is an adjective of (جنات). (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَيَأْكُلُونَ كَما تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعامُ وَالنَّارُ مَثْوىً لَهُمْ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; the clause (يتمتعون) is the khabar of (الذين); the clause (يأكلون) is conjoined to the clause (يتمتعون). (كما) is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), according to the school of most grammarians, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), according to the school of Sībawayh. (تأكل الأنعام) is a verb and its agent. The wāw is resumptive; (النار) is a mubtadaʾ, (مثوى) a khabar, and (لهم) an adjective of (مثوى).

dervis-irab:13-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آسِنٍ) With the long and the short vowel [āsin / asin], like ḍārib and ḥadhir; i.e. unaltered, unlike the water of this world, which changes because of the accidents that befall it. In al-Mukhtār: «Al-āsin, of water, is like al-ājin in form and meaning (stagnant, brackish); asana, of the pattern ḍaraba and dakhala; and asina, so it is āsin, of the pattern ṭariba, is a dialectal form of it.» One says: the water asana and ajana when its taste and smell change. A verse by Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya was recited:
لقد سقتني رضابا غير ذي أسن ... كالمسك فتّ على ماء العناقيد
(She gave me to drink a saliva without staleness, like musk crumbled onto the juice of grape clusters.)
(عَسَلٍ) They transmitted both masculine and feminine for al-ʿasal (honey), and in the Qur'an it comes as masculine in His words (من عسل مصفى). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-ʿasal is masculine and feminine — and that is the more common — and its diminutive is ʿusayla, according to the feminine usage, on the view that it is a portion of the genus and a part of it.» In al-Mukhtār: «Al-ʿasal is masculine and feminine; from it one says ʿasala al-ṭaʿām, i.e. he prepared it with honey, of the patterns ḍaraba and naṣara; zanjabīl muʿassal, i.e. ginger prepared with honey; al-ʿāsil is the one who takes honey from the beehive; and the bees are ʿassāla.» In al-Asās: «The guide trots (yaʿsilu) in the desert; the winds struck the water so that it ripples (yaʿsilu ʿasalānan). Al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
قد صبّحت والظل غض ما رحل ... حوضا كأن ماءه إذا عسل
من نافض الريح رويزيّ سمل
(She came in the morning, while the shade was still fresh and had not departed, to a trough whose water, when it rippled from the shaking of the wind, was like a worn Rūzī garment.)
A quivering spear and a trotting wolf (ʿassāl), and quivering spears and trotting wolves (ʿawāsil). And you say: "the trotting one gathers in the shade as the honey-gatherer collects the honey"; and "the Banū so-and-so hasten to the ʿassāla as the bees speed to the ʿassāla", which is the hive. Food maʿsūl and muʿassal; and ʿasaltu al-qawm and ʿassaltuhum: I fed them honey.»

* I'rab:
(وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ هِيَ أَشَدُّ قُوَّةً مِنْ قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتِي أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْناهُمْ فَلا ناصِرَ لَهُمْ) Resumptive speech, introduced to console him ﷺ, serving as an example for him. (كأين) is predicative (khabariyya); it is a word compounded of the kāf and (أي), in the sense of the predicative kam, and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (من قرية) is its tamyīz (specification) — the discussion of it has been given in detail before, so refresh your memory of it. (هي) is a mubtadaʾ and (أشد) a khabar (predicate), and the clause is an adjective of (قرية); (قوة) is a tamyīz; (من قريتك) are attached to (أشد); (التي) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قريتك), and the clause (أخرجتك) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (التي). The clause (أهلكناهم) is the khabar of (كأين). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (ناصر) is its noun and (لهم) its khabar. From Ibn ʿAbbās: when the Prophet ﷺ left Mecca for the cave, he turned towards Mecca and said: «You are the dearest of Allah's lands to me, and were it not that your people drove me out of you, I would not have left. The most insolent of enemies is one who is insolent towards Allah in His sanctuary, or kills one other than his killer, or kills by entering the Jāhiliyya.» [Translator's note: so printed; the last phrase is known in the ḥadīth as «or kills for the blood-feuds of the Jāhiliyya» (bi-dhuḥūl al-jāhiliyya).] (أَفَمَنْ كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ) Resumptive speech, introduced to begin explaining the state of the two groups, the believers and the disbelievers. The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied element required by the context, the implied form being "Is the matter not as mentioned? So is one who stands firm on a clear proof and evidence like one to whom [the evil of his deeds] has been made attractive?" (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (كان) is a defective past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", referring to (من); (على بيّنة) is the khabar; (من ربه) is an adjective of (بينة); (كمن) is the khabar [of من]; the clause (زين), in the passive, is the ṣila; (له) are attached to (زين); (سوء عمله) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (اتبعوا) is conjoined to (زين), and in it the meaning of (من) is observed, just as its wording was observed in (زين); and (أهواءهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ فِيها أَنْهارٌ مِنْ ماءٍ غَيْرِ آسِنٍ وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ طَعْمُهُ وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ خَمْرٍ لَذَّةٍ لِلشَّارِبِينَ) (مثل الجنة) is a mubtadaʾ — the discussion of its khabar will come; (التي) is an adjective, and the clause (وعد المتقون) is the ṣila. (فيها) is a fronted khabar and (أنهار) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الجنة), or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it — in it are rivers", or it falls within the domain of the ṣila as a repetition of it. (من ماء) is an adjective of (أنهار), and (غير آسن) a second adjective of (أنهار); (أنهار) is conjoined to the first (أنهار); (من خمر) is a naʿt, and (لذة للشاربين) a second naʿt; (للشاربين) are attached to (لذة) because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of taking pleasure, and it occurs as an adjective of the wine. It may also be the feminine of ladhdh, ladhdh meaning ladhīdh (delicious); on the first view it must be interpreted as a derived word so that it can validly serve as an adjective, in the manner of "Zayd is justice" meaning "just". More discussion of (لذة للشاربين) will come in the section on Benefits. [Translator's note: the Benefits section below does not in fact discuss (لذة للشاربين).] (وَأَنْهارٌ مِنْ عَسَلٍ مُصَفًّى وَلَهُمْ فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) (أنهار) is conjoined to the preceding (أنهار); (من عسل) is an adjective, and (مصفّى) is an adjective of (عسل). The wāw is a conjunction; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (فيها) are attached to what the khabar is attached to, namely the omitted [notion of] being established; the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being "kinds"; and (من كل الثمرات) is a naʿt of the omitted mubtadaʾ. (مغفرة) is conjoined to "kinds", or it is a mubtadaʾ whose fronted khabar is omitted, i.e. "and they have forgiveness"; and (من ربهم) is a naʿt of (مغفرة). (كَمَنْ هُوَ خالِدٌ فِي النَّارِ وَسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيماً فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعاءَهُمْ) (كمن) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "Is one who abides eternally in this Garden, according to what the promise stated, like one who abides eternally in the Fire?" On this view the khabar of (مثل) is implied: Sībawayh supplied it as "among what is recited to you is the description of the Garden", with the clause after it also explaining the description; al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl supplied it as "the description of the Garden is what you hear", with the clause after it also explanatory. It is also permissible for the khabar to be (كمن هو خالد في النار). (وسقوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (سقوا) is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; (ماء) is a second object, and (حميما) a naʿt of (ماء). (فقطع): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قطع أمعاءهم) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object.

* Benefits:
Much has been said, and at length, about this verse. We shall quote al-Zamakhsharī's wording, together with a splendid comment on it. He said: «If you say: what is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: (مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون فيها أنهار)? I say: it is speech in the form of an affirmation with the meaning of negation and disapproval, because it is enfolded under the ruling of a speech headed by the particle of disapproval, entering its domain and being strung on its thread — namely His words, Exalted is He: (أفمن كان على بيّنة من ربه كمن زيّن له سوء عمله). So it is as though it were said: "Is the description of the Garden like one who abides eternally in the Fire?", i.e. like the description of the recompense of one who abides eternally in the Fire. If you say: then why was it stripped of the particle of disapproval, and what is the benefit of the stripping? I say: stripping it of the particle of disapproval adds to the depiction of the obstinacy of one who equates the one who holds fast to clear proof with the one who follows his whims, and shows that he is in the position of one who affirms equality between the Garden in which those rivers flow and the Fire whose people are given boiling water to drink. Its counterpart is the poet's saying:
أفرح أن أرزأ الكرام وأن ... أورث ذودا شصائصا نبلا
([Should] I rejoice at being bereaved of the noble ones, and at inheriting a few dry, worthless she-camels?)
It is speech disapproving of rejoicing at the loss of the noble and the inheriting of the camels, though stripped of the particle of disapproval, because it is enfolded under the ruling of the saying of one who said: "Do you rejoice at your brother's death and at inheriting his camels?" What the particle of disapproval was dropped for is the intention to depict the ugliness of what he was suspected of; so it is as though he said to him: "Yes, the like of me rejoices at the loss of the noble and at [Translator's note: printed «بأبن», apparently for «بأن», "that"] he gets in exchange for them a few camels of little worth!" — and this is of the kind of concession under which lies every disapproval.»
Ibn al-Munayyir, the author of al-Intiṣāf, commented on al-Zamakhsharī's words, saying: «How much people have said in interpreting this verse! Yet I have not seen anything more elegant or sweeter than these subtle points he mentioned. They lack only the note that there is something omitted in the speech that must be supplied, because there is no equivalence between the Garden and those abiding eternally in the Fire except by supplying "the like of one dwelling in it", which sets the balance of the speech right and makes its two pans equal. Of this kind are His words, Exalted is He: (أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله), for something omitted must be supplied with the first or the second so that the two parts are equal. By what I have supplied in the verse, the end of the speech fits its beginning, so that what is intended is to compare the remoteness of equality between the one holding fast to the evil [Translator's note: printed «بالسيئة»; the context requires «بالبيّنة», "the clear proof"] and the one riding his whims with the remoteness of equality between the one blessed in the Garden and the one punished in the Fire, in the corresponding attributes mentioned on the two sides. It is of the kind of comparing a thing with itself in respect of two states, one of which is clearer in exposition than the other: for the one holding fast to the Sunna is the one blessed in the Garden so described, and the follower of whims is the one punished in the Fire so described. But He disapproved of equating them in respect of deeds first, and made that clear by disapproving of equating them in respect of recompense second.»

dervis-irab:16-19.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ حَتَّى إِذا خَرَجُوا مِنْ عِنْدِكَ قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ: ماذا قالَ آنِفاً) A resumptive discourse, introduced to explain another aspect of their mockery and obstinacy: they used to attend the assembly of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and hear his words without retaining them or paying them any heed; then, when they left the assembly, they asked the people of knowledge among the Companions, in mockery, "What did he say just now?" It is also said that this was during the Friday sermon, in which case the verse would be Madinan. «ومنهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «من» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «يستمع إليك» is a ṣila (relative clause), and the wording of «من» has been observed (i.e. the singular is used). «حتى» is a particle of limit and of genitive. «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition. The clause «خرجوا» is in the position of a genitive, through the adverb's annexation to it. «من عندك» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خرجوا». The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. «للذين» is attached to «قالوا». The clause «أوتوا», in the passive, is a ṣila; the «و» is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and «العلم» is a second direct object. As for «ماذا», it was previously noted that there are two analyses of it: «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» is a relative noun, here specifically, in the position of nominative as khabar; or you may take the whole of it as a single interrogative noun. «آنفا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «قال», i.e. "starting afresh" (muʾtanifan). Al-Zamakhsharī and Abu al-Baqāʾ analysed it as an adverb, i.e. "what did he say just now?". Abu Hayyān rejected this and said: "We do not know of any grammarian who counted it among the adverbs." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The exegetes say that «آنفا» means 'the hour just past, close to us', and this is an explanation by meaning." In al-Qāmūs it says: "He said «آنِفاً» (with the pattern of ṣāḥib and katif; and it is read with both forms), i.e. 'since an hour ago', that is, 'in the first period of time close to us'", as though inclining to its being accusative as an adverb. Al-Zajjāj said: "It derives from «استأنفتُ الشيء» ('I began the thing'), and the meaning is: 'What did he say in the first period of time close to us?'" On this basis the scale tipped in favour of those who say it is an adverb.
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ) «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذين» is its khabar. The clause «طبع الله على قلوبهم» is a ṣila. The clause «واتبعوا أهواءهم» is likewise conjoined and falls within the scope of the ṣila.
(وَالَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زادَهُمْ هُدىً وَآتاهُمْ تَقْواهُمْ) «والذين» is a mubtadaʾ. The clause «اهتدوا» is a ṣila. The clause «زادهم» is the khabar. «هدى» is a second direct object or a tamyīz (specification). «وآتاهم» is conjoined to «زادهم», and «تقواهم» is a second direct object. «تقواهم» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent.
(فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً) The «فاء» is resumptive. «هل» is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation. «ينظرون» is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the «و» is the fāʿil (agent). «إلا» is a particle of restriction and «الساعة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «أن تأتيهم» is an interpreted maṣdar, a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «الساعة», i.e. "the matter is nothing other than its coming upon them". «بغتة» is a ḥāl.
(فَقَدْ جاءَ أَشْراطُها فَأَنَّى لَهُمْ إِذا جاءَتْهُمْ ذِكْراهُمْ) The «فاء» expresses causation for the Hour's coming suddenly; the connection between the two is the connection of cause to effect. «قد» is a particle of certainty. «أشراطها» is the fāʿil; it is the plural of «شَرَط» (with two fatḥas), which is "sign". It says in al-Miṣbāḥ: "The plural of «الشَّرْط» is «شروط», like «فلس» and «فلوس»; and «الشَّرَط» (with two fatḥas) is the sign, its plural being «أشراط», like «سبب» and «أسباب»; from it comes «أشراط الساعة», i.e. its signs." «فأنى»: the «فاء» is a conjunction, and «أنى» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. «ذكراهم» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, i.e. "how can remembrance be theirs?". The clause «إذا» and what follows it is parenthetical, and the apodosis of «إذا» is omitted, its implied form being "how will they remember?". It is also permissible that the mubtadaʾ is the omitted element, i.e. "how can deliverance be theirs?", and «ذكراهم» would then be the fāʿil of «جاءتهم».
(فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنْبِكَ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ) The «فاء» is the «fāʾ al-faṣīḥa» (the eloquent fāʾ), because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if you have come to know the felicity of the believers and the wretchedness of the disbelievers, then stand firm in what you already hold of knowledge of the Oneness, for it alone avails on the Day of Resurrection, and in humility and self-abasement by seeking forgiveness for your sin and the sins of those who believe in your message". «أن» and what is in its scope stand in the place of the two objects of «اعلم». «أن» and its noun (ism), and the clause «لا إله إلا الله» is its khabar. The discussion of the i'rab of the testimony of faith has already been given at length. «استغفر» is an imperative verb. «لذنبك» is attached to «استغفر». «وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات» is conjoined to «لذنبك».
(وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمْ وَمَثْواكُمْ) The «واو» is resumptive. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يعلم» is the khabar. «متقلبكم» is a mafʿūl bihi, and «مثواكم» is conjoined to «متقلبكم». Their meanings are "your movement about" and "your abode". Al-Zamakhsharī's wording is: "Allah knows your states and your comings and goings, and your moving about in your livelihoods and your trades." It is permissible for both to be mīmī maṣdars (verbal nouns with prefixed mīm) from «تقلّب» and «ثوى», and for both to be nouns of place or of time.

* Benefits:
Maṣdars have often come as ḥāl in indefinite form, and in this there is one irregularity, namely that it is a maṣdar. The basic rule was that they should not occur as ḥāl, because they differ in meaning from their ḥāl-owner; but since they (the Arabs) often predicate maṣdars of persons, as an extension, as in «زيد عدل» ("Zayd is justice"), they did the same here, since this is better than predication, as in «طلع زيد بغتة» ("Zayd appeared suddenly"), «جاء ركضا» ("he came running") and «قتلته صبرا» ("I killed him in captivity"). As for «صبرا», it is that one keeps him alive in confinement and then shoots at him until he is killed; it is a ḥāl from the object of «قتلته». All of that is on the interpretation as a descriptive; so «بغتة» is interpreted as the description of one who takes by surprise, since it means "surprise", i.e. "surprising" (mubāghitan), or from «بغت», i.e. "taking by surprise". One says «بغتة», i.e. «فجأة», and «البغت» is the sudden surprise. The poet said:
ولكنهم كانوا ولم أدر بغتة ... وأعظم شيء حين يفجؤك البغت
(But they came to be, without my knowing, suddenly; and the greatest of things is when the sudden surprise takes you unawares.)
Despite the frequency of this, Sībawayh and the majority said that it is not subject to analogy at all, whether it is a species of its governing verb or not, just as the maṣdar occurring as an adjective or a khabar is not subject to analogy, on account of the shared abstract descriptive sense. Al-Mubarrad applied analogy to it where it is a species of the verb governing it, because it then indicates the manner by itself; so he permitted by analogy «جاء زيد سرعة» ("Zayd came speed"), since speed is a species of coming, and forbade «جاء ضحكا» ("he came laughing"), since laughing is not a species of coming.
Ibn Hishām said in al-Ḥawāshī: "Al-Mubarrad applied analogy to it and Sībawayh did not, because Sībawayh holds that it is a ḥāl by interpretation, and putting a maṣdar in the place of a descriptive is not subject to analogy, just as its reverse is not; whereas al-Mubarrad holds that it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing verb has been omitted on the strength of an indication, so it is subject to analogy in his view, just as the governing verb of all the other objects is omitted on the strength of an indication. This disagreement is therefore built upon the disagreement as to whether it is a ḥāl or a mafʿūl muṭlaq."
Al-Laqqānī said: "Giving examples with «بغتة», «ركضا» and «صبرا» does not show that this is the necessary analysis for them; rather it is permissible to make them absolute objects, since they are a species of their governing verb, like «رجع القهقرى» ('he went back backwards')."
Ibn Mālik in al-Tashīl, and his son in his commentary on the Alfiyya, applied analogy to the ḥāl after «أما», as in «أما علما فعالم» ("As for knowledge, he is a knowledgeable man"). The origin of this is that a man had a person described in his presence as knowledgeable or otherwise, and said to the describer: «أما علما فعالم», i.e. "whenever a person is mentioned in respect of knowledge, the one mentioned is knowledgeable", as though denying what the person was described with other than knowledge. On this analysis the ḥāl-owner is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the governor of the ḥāl is «يُذكر», given the established rule that the governor of the ḥāl-owner is the governor of the ḥāl. It is also permissible that the governor of the ḥāl be what follows the fāʾ, if it is fit to act upon what precedes it, and its owner be the pronoun contained in it; the ḥāl on this view is a confirmatory one (muʾakkida), and the implied sense is "whatever there may be, the one mentioned is, in a state of knowledge...". If what follows the fāʾ cannot act upon what precedes it, it must be accusative by the protasis verb implied after «أما», as in «أما علما فلا علم له», «أما علما فإن له علما» and «أما علما فهو ذو علم», because a maṣdar can act on what precedes it. If the maṣdar following «أما» is defined by «ال», then in Sībawayh's view it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Akhfash held that both the one defined by «ال» and the indefinite one after «أما» are a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and the Kufans held that both are a mafʿūl bihi of an implied verb, the implied sense being "whatever knowledge you mention, the one you described is knowledgeable". Ibn Mālik said in Sharḥ al-Tashīl: "This view is, in my opinion, the more likely to be correct and the most deserving of reliance in the answer." Ibn Mālik and his son also applied analogy after a khabar to which its mubtadaʾ is likened, as in «زيد زهير شعرا»: «زهير» (in diminutive form) is a khabar to which its mubtadaʾ «زيد» is likened, the implied sense being "like Zuhayr in poetry"; «مثل» was omitted only so that the wording of comparison disappear and the speech be more eloquent. «شعرا» is a ḥāl in the implied sense of a description, i.e. "a poet", and its governor is the sense of a verb contained in «زهير», since its meaning is "excellent"; the ḥāl-owner is the latent pronoun in «زهير», given the established rule that a rigid noun interpreted as a derived one carries a pronoun. It is also permissible that «شعرا» be a tamyīz for what was vague in the omitted «مثل», which is its governor; this was said by al-Khaṣṣāf in al-Īḍāḥ, and Abu Hayyān in al-Irtishāf and Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī thought it the more apparent, and al-Laqqānī preferred it: "The most apparent is that it is a tamyīz converted from the agent, the original being «زيد مماثل شعره شعر زهير» ('Zayd, his poetry is like Zuhayr's poetry')."
They also applied analogy to it after a khabar accompanied by «ال» that indicates perfection, as in:
أنت الرجل علما — here «علما» is a ḥāl, and its governor is the sense of a verb contained in «الرجل», since its meaning is "the perfect". In Ibn Jinnī's al-Khāṭirīyāt: "«أنت الرجل فهما وأدبا» admits two analyses: one is that in your saying «أنت الرجل» there is the sense of a verb, i.e. 'you are the perfect one in understanding and refinement'; the second is that it is in the sense of 'you understand with understanding and show refinement with refinement'." Abu Hayyān said in al-Irtishāf: "In my view it is possible that it is a tamyīz, as though he had said «أنت الكامل أدبا», i.e. 'his refinement', so it is converted from the agent." So three opinions result for it: ḥāl, mafʿūl muṭlaq and tamyīz. From the disagreement about the accusative maṣdar the following views result:
1- The view of Sībawayh: the maṣdar is the ḥāl.
2- The view of al-Mubarrad and al-Akhfash: it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq not made accusative by the verb before it, but by its governor omitted from its own wording, and that omitted element is the ḥāl.
3- The view of the Kufans: it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is the verb mentioned, and it is not in the position of ḥāl.
4- A group held that it is a maṣdar with an omitted muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), and the implied form of «جاء ركضا» is «جاء ذا ركض» ("he came possessing running").
On the view that it is a ḥāl there are further positions: 1- The view of Sībawayh: no analogy. 2- Al-Mubarrad held it subject to analogy where it is a species of its governor. 3- Ibn Mālik and his son applied analogy in three cases: (a) after «إما» [Translator's note: the source writes «إما» here, whereas the discussion above has «أما»]; (b) after a khabar to which its mubtadaʾ is likened; (c) where the khabar is accompanied by «ال» indicating perfection.

dervis-irab:20-28.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْلا نُزِّلَتْ سُورَةٌ) A resumptive discourse, to explain the stance of the truthful believers and of the hypocrites regarding jihad. The believers asked their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to send down upon His Messenger ﷺ a sūra in which He would command them to fight the disbelievers, out of their eagerness for jihad and for attaining the abundant reward that Allah has prepared for the mujāhidīn; so Allah related this about them. «يقول» is an imperfect verb and «الذين» is its fāʿil (agent); the clause «آمنوا» is a ṣila (relative clause). «لولا» is a particle of urging, meaning «هلّا» ("why not"). «نزلت» is a passive past verb and «سورة» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(فَإِذا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُحْكَمَةٌ وَذُكِرَ فِيهَا الْقِتالُ رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ نَظَرَ الْمَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ فَأَوْلى لَهُمْ) The «فاء» is a conjunction. «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition. The clause «أنزلت» is in the position of a genitive through the adverb's annexation to it; it is a passive past verb and «سورة» is the nāʾib fāʿil. «محكمة» is a naʿt (adjective), i.e. "clear, not ambiguous, admitting no interpretation other than the obligation of fighting". From Qatāda: every sūra in which fighting is mentioned is muḥkama (firm), because abrogation does not apply to it. «وذكر» is conjoined to «أنزلت»; «فيها» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ذكر»; «القتال» is the nāʾib fāʿil. The clause «رأيت» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. «الذين» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «في قلوبهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مرض» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); this nominal clause has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. «ينظرون» is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the «و» is the fāʿil. The clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) if the seeing is by sight, and as a second direct object if the seeing is of the heart; both aspects are intended in the verse. «إليك» is attached to «ينظرون». «نظر المغشي» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of emphasis. «عليه» is attached to «المغشي», since it is a passive participle; «من الموت» is also attached to «المغشي». «فأولى»: the «فاء» is resumptive. As for «أولى لهم», al-Jawharī said: "The Arabs say «أولى لك» as a threat and a menace. Then the lexicographers and the grammarians differed over this word. Al-Aṣmaʿī said that it is a past verb meaning 'what destroys him has drawn near to him'; most say that it is a noun. These then differed: it was said that it is derived from «الولي», which is nearness, and it was said that it is from «الويل» (woe). That concerns its derivation and meaning. As for the i'rab, if we say that it is a noun, there are several aspects. The first is that it is a mubtadaʾ and «لهم» its khabar, the implied sense being 'destruction is for them'; Abu al-Baqāʾ confined himself to this. The second is that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, the implied sense being 'punishment' or 'destruction is nearer to them', i.e. closer and nearer; and it is permissible that the lām mean «الباء», i.e. 'more fitting and more deserving for them'. The third is that it is a mubtadaʾ with «لهم» attached to it, the lām meaning «الباء», and «طاعة» its khabar, the implied sense being 'more fitting for them is obedience, rather than anything else'. If we adopt the view of al-Aṣmaʿī, it is a past verb whose fāʿil is an implied element indicated by the context, as though it were said 'so it drew near, it, i.e. destruction'. This is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording, where he said that its meaning is a prayer against them, that destruction may draw near them. Al-Mubarrad said: it is said to one who intended to be angry and then slipped away, «أولى لك», i.e. 'anger drew near you'." Abu Hayyān said: "The author of al-Ṣiḥāḥ said: the Arabs' saying «أولى لك» is a threat and a menace, and from it is the poet's saying:
فأولى ثم أولى ثم أولى ... وهل للداء يحلب من يرد
(Closer, then closer, then closer — and can the one who wants to be milked of the disease be turned back?)
They differed as to whether it is a noun or a verb. Al-Aṣmaʿī held that it means 'what destroys him has drawn near to him', i.e. has come down upon him, and he recited:
تعادى بين هاديتين منها ... وأولى أن يزيد على الثلاث
(She ran between two leaders [fore-necks] of hers, and it came close to exceeding three.)
i.e. it came close to exceeding. Thaʿlab said: no one has said anything better than what al-Aṣmaʿī said. Al-Mubarrad said: it is said to one who intended ruin, as it is related that a Bedouin used to shoot at game continually and it would escape him, and he would say «أولى لك رمي صيدا», meaning that he drew near to it and then it escaped him; and he said:
فلو كان أولى يطعم القوم صيدهم ... ولكن أولى يترك القوم جوّعا
(If «أولى» fed the people their game... but «أولى» leaves the people hungry.)
Most hold that it is a noun. It was said that it is derived from «الولي», meaning nearness, as the poet said: تكلفني ليلى وقد شطّ وليّها ... وعادت عواد بيننا وخطوب (Laylā burdens me while her nearness has become distant, and obstacles and calamities have come between us). Al-Jurjānī said: it is what was converted from «الويل», so it is an afʿal form of it, but with a transposition in it." Al-Jalāl said in his commentary on Sūrat al-Qiyāma: "The word is a noun of a verb (ism fiʿl) and the lām is for clarification", i.e. it is indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, with no grammatical position, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun referring back to what is understood from the context, namely that this word is used in praying for something disliked; his saying "for clarification" refers to the object, and in meaning it is redundant, like «سقيا لك». The wording of al-Qāmūs is: "«وأولى لك» is a word of threat and menace, and the meaning is: 'evil has drawn near you, so beware'." Its commentator said: "It was also said that its meaning is 'woe to you', or 'may Allah bring you what you dislike', in which case the lām is redundant."
(طاعَةٌ وَقَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ فَإِذا عَزَمَ الْأَمْرُ فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا اللَّهَ لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ) «طاعة وقول» is an independent discourse from which one of the two parts has been omitted: either the khabar, the implied form being "better" (amthal), which is the view of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl; or the mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "the matter" or "our matter is obedience". It was mentioned earlier that it may be the khabar of «أولى», and there are other analyses there which we have set aside because of their remoteness and strained nature. «فإذا»: the «فاء» is a conjunction and «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to «صدقوا», as in «إذا جاءني بطعام فلو جئتني أطعمتك». The clause «عزم الأمر» is in the position of a genitive through the adverb's annexation to it. The «فاء» links the apodosis of «إذا»; «لو» is a non-jussive conditional; «صدقوا» is a verb and fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of «إذا». The majestic name is a mafʿūl bihi. In «لكان», the lām falls in the apodosis of «لو»; «كان» is a defective past verb whose ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", i.e. truthfulness; «خيرا» is its khabar, and «لهم» is attached to «خيرا».
(فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ) The «فاء» is resumptive. «عسيتم» is a past verb of the verbs of hope, and the «تاء» is its ism; more discussion of it will come in the section on benefits. «إن» is conditional and «توليتم» is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The apodosis is omitted, being indicated by «فهل عسيتم», or it is «فهل عسيتم» itself according to one who holds that it may be fronted. The clause of the protasis and its apodosis is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. «أن تفسدوا» is the khabar of «عسى», and «في الأرض» is attached to «تفسدوا».
(وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحامَكُمْ) Conjoined to «أن تفسدوا في الأرض».
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وَأَعْمى أَبْصارَهُمْ) «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذين» is its khabar. The clause «لعنهم الله» is a ṣila. The «فاء» is a conjunction; «أصمهم» is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; «أعمى أبصارهم» is conjoined to «فأصمهم».
(أَفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ أَمْ عَلى قُلُوبٍ أَقْفالُها) The hamza is for a rebuking interrogative, and the «فاء» is conjoined to an implied element required by the context. «لا» is a negative particle; «يتدبرون القرآن» is an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. «أم» is munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), meaning «بل»; and the hamza is to record against them that their hearts are locked, so that no remembrance reaches them. «على قلوب» is a fronted khabar and «أقفالها» a mubtadaʾ necessarily postponed. The secret of the indefiniteness will come in the section on rhetoric.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ ارْتَدُّوا عَلى أَدْبارِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْهُدَى الشَّيْطانُ سَوَّلَ لَهُمْ وَأَمْلى لَهُمْ) «إن» is a particle resembling the verb, and «الذين» is its ism; the clause «ارتدوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun. «على أدبارهم» is a ḥāl, and «من بعد» is attached to «ارتدوا». «ما» is maṣdarī (verbal-noun-forming), and «ما» with what is in its scope is in the position of a genitive through annexation to the adverb. «لهم» is attached to «تبين», and «الهدى» is the fāʿil. «الشيطان» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «سول لهم» is the khabar of «الشيطان»; the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن». The meaning of «سوّل لهم» is "made easy for them", from «السول», which is slackness. «وأملى لهم» is conjoined to «سول لهم».
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قالُوا لِلَّذِينَ كَرِهُوا ما نَزَّلَ اللَّهُ سَنُطِيعُكُمْ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَمْرِ) «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «بأنهم» is its khabar. «أن» and its ism, and the clause «قالوا» is its khabar. «للذين» is attached to «قالوا»; the clause «كرهوا» is a ṣila; «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause «نزل الله» is a ṣila. The clause «سنطيعكم» is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). «في بعض الأمر» is attached to «نطيعكم».
(وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِسْرارَهُمْ) The «واو» is for ḥāl. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يعلم إسرارهم» is the khabar; «إسرارهم» is a mafʿūl bihi. It is with kasra on the hamza, a maṣdar of «أسرّ»; and it was read with fatḥa, the plural of «سر» ("secret").
(فَكَيْفَ إِذا تَوَفَّتْهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبارَهُمْ) The «فاء» is a conjunction. «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, i.e. "what is their state?"; it may also be analysed as an object of an omitted verb, i.e. "how will they act?". «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the omitted mubtadaʾ. The clause «توفتهم الملائكة» is in the position of a genitive through the adverb's annexation to it. The clause «يضربون» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil or from the object. «وجوههم» is a mafʿūl bihi and «وأدبارهم» is conjoined to «وجوههم».
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ اتَّبَعُوا ما أَسْخَطَ اللَّهَ وَكَرِهُوا رِضْوانَهُ فَأَحْبَطَ أَعْمالَهُمْ) «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «بأنهم» is the khabar. The clause «اتبعوا» is the khabar of «أن». «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi and the clause «أسخط الله» is a ṣila. «وكرهوا رضوانه» is conjoined to the clause «اتبعوا ما أسخط الله». «فأحبط» is conjoined to what precedes, and «أعمالهم» is a mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, Exalted is He, «فهل عسيتم إن توليتم» to the end of the verse, there is an iltifāt (shift of address) from the third person to the second. The discussion of iltifāt was given at length earlier. The secret in it here is that it came to reinforce the rebuke, intensify the censure, and record it against them directly, by address. Someone may ask: how can the interrogative be valid from Allah, Exalted is He, when He knows what has been and what will be? The answer is that, since it was known of you that you are likely to be told by everyone who has sounded your depths and knows your sickness and the looseness of your bond in faith: "O these people, what do you think? Is it to be expected of you, if you take charge of the people's affairs and their concerns are entrusted to you and you become rulers, that you will cause corruption in the land through vying with one another for kingship, craving for this world, mutual quarrelling and plunder, and cutting of kinship ties by some fighting their relatives, burying girls alive, taking bribes and returning to the first Jāhiliyya?"
2- Indefiniteness and metaphor: in His saying, Exalted is He: «أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها», there is the indefiniteness of «قلوب» together with the annexation of the locks to it, by way of the implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). As for the indefiniteness, it is either to make their condition dreadful, as though it were said "upon hearts unknown, whose matter is obscure", or because what is meant by it is the hearts of some of them, namely the hearts of the hypocrites. As for the metaphor, it is that He likened their hearts to chests (boxes) and borrowed for them something of their concomitants, namely the locks that are particular to them, to suggest that opening them is remote and that their closure is continuous, so that their hidden contents are disclosed to no one and no one is made aware of their hidden contents.

* Benefits:
It is permissible to put kasra on the sīn of «عسى» in the dialect of one who says «هو عسِيَ بكذا», like «شجِيَ» from «شجا». This permissibility is not absolute, whether you attribute it to an overt noun or a pronoun; rather it is restricted to its being attributed to a pronoun with which the end of the verb takes sukūn, such as the tāʾ, the nūn or «نا». It was read with both in the Seven: Nāfiʿ read it with kasra, for the sake of harmony with the «ياء», and the rest read it with fatḥa, which is the preferred one, because it is current on tongues.

dervis-irab:29-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَضْغانَهُمْ) Their grudges. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«ضَغِنَ صدرُه ضَغَنًا» (of the pattern tabiʿa) means 'he bore a grudge'; the noun is «ضِغْن» and the plural is «أضغان», like «حِمْل» and «أحمال»; he is «ضَغِن» and «ضاغِن»." ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
وإن الضغن بعد الضغن يبدو ... عليك ويخرج الداء الدفينا
(Grudge after grudge will show itself against you, and bring out the buried disease.)
Among the wonders of the letters ḍād and ghayn is that when they come together as the fāʾ and ʿayn of a word they indicate closely related meanings, namely something hidden away in concealment, as was said of «الضغن». One says «ضَغِن عليَّ فلان واضطغن» ("so-and-so bore a grudge against me"); "may Allah remove every one who harbours a grudge against his brother and nurses enmity toward his allies"; "I kept at him until I drew out the rest of his grudge and emptied his heart of what it had contained". «ضغبت الأرنب» means the hare cried out when seized. «ضربه بضِغث» means with a handful of small twigs or grass, some of it within the other; and from its figurative use comes «هذه أضغاث أحلام» ("these are confused dreams"), which is what is jumbled and hidden of them. «ضَغَط الشيء» is to squeeze it and to constrict it; "I seek refuge in Allah from the squeezing of the grave", which is hidden, known only to Allah. "I heard the «ضَغيل» of the cupper", which is the sound of his sucking; «ضَغَمَه ضَغمةَ الأسد» is the bite of the lion with a full mouth; and its «ضَيْغَم» and «ضَياغِمة» is the lion. «ضغا فلان ضغاءً» means he writhed from a blow or harm; and you say «أضغيتُه إضغاءً» and then «أغضيتُ عنه إغضاءً» ("I overlooked him"); "his children spent the night «يتغاضَون» from hunger and «يتضاغَون»" — and this is among the greatest wonders.
(بِسِيماهُمْ) By their sign. In al-Qāmūs: "«السَّومة» with ḍamma, and «السِّيمة», «السِّيماء» and «السِّيمياء» with kasra: the sign."
(لَحْنِ الْقَوْلِ) Its manner and style. It was also said that «اللحن» is that you «تلحن» in your speech, i.e. incline it toward some manner so that your addressee perceives it, like allusion and double meaning. He said:
ولقد لحنت لكم لكيما تفهموا ... واللحن يعرفه ذوي الألباب
(I spoke to you allusively so that you might understand; and allusion is recognised by people of intellect.)
So «اللحن» is turning speech away from the overt sense, and the one who makes a mistake is also «لاحن» because he turns away from what is correct; i.e. "so that you understand, and not others, for allusion is recognised by the people of intellect and not by others". It says in al-Miṣbāḥ: "«اللَّحَن» (with two fatḥas) is perceptiveness; it is a maṣdar of the pattern tabiʿa, and the agent is «لَحِن». It is made transitive with the hamza, so one says «ألحنتُه فلَحِن», i.e. 'I made him perceptive and he became perceptive'; it is quickness of understanding. «هو ألحن من زيد» means 'quicker in understanding'. «لَحَنَ في كلامه لَحْنًا» (of the pattern nafaʿa) means 'he made a mistake in Arabic'. Abū Zayd said: «لحن في كلامه لحنًا» with sukūn on the ḥāʾ, and «لحونًا», when he made a mistake in the case endings and departed from the correct form. «لحنتُ بلحن فلان لحنًا» also means 'I spoke in his dialect'. «لحنتُ له لحنًا» means 'I said a saying that he understood from me and that remained hidden from others of the people'. «فهمته من لحن كلامه وفحواه ومعاريضه» are of one meaning." Al-Azharī said: "«لحن القول» is like the title; it is like a sign to which you point so that the addressee perceives your purpose."
The summary is that «اللحن» has two meanings, a correct one and a mistaken one. The correct one is turning speech and moving it from explicit statement to implication and allusion, and this is praiseworthy from the standpoint of eloquence. From it is his saying ﷺ: "Perhaps some of you are more eloquent («ألحن») in his argument than others." The poet said:
منطق صائب وتلحن أحيا ... نا وخير الحديث ما كان لحنا
(His speech is sound, and sometimes you speak allusively; and the best of talk is what is allusive.)
This is what is meant by His saying «ولتعرفنهم في لحن القول». As for the blameworthy «لحن», it is evident: turning speech from what is correct to what is mistaken, by dropping the case endings or by misreading. The meaning of the verse: "And you, Muḥammad, will surely recognise the hypocrites by what they hint at in speech, by disparaging your cause and the cause of the Muslims, deprecating it and mocking it." After this no hypocrite spoke in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ without his recognising him by his speech and inferring from the drift of his words the corruption of his inner self and his hypocrisy.

* I'rab:
(أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ أَنْ لَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللَّهُ أَضْغانَهُمْ) «أم» is a particle of disavowal and conjunction. «حسب الذين» is a verb and fāʿil (agent). «في قلوبهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مرض» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «أن» and what is within its scope stand in the place of the two objects of «حسب». «أن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», and its ism is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and future. «يخرج» is an imperfect verb, accusative by «لن», and the clause is the khabar of «أن». «الله» is the fāʿil and «أضغانهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَأَرَيْناكَهُمْ فَلَعَرَفْتَهُمْ بِسِيماهُمْ) The «واو» is a conjunction, «لو» is conditional, and «نشاء» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we". The lām falls in the apodosis of «لو». «أريناكهم» is a past verb; «نا» is the fāʿil, the «كاف» is the first object and the «هاء» the second object. The seeing here is by sight, which is why it takes only two objects. The «فاء» is a conjunction, and the lām is conjoined to the first lām that falls in the apodosis, and was repeated for emphasis. «عرفتهم» is a verb, fāʿil and object. The clause «لأريناكهم» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of «لو», and the clause «فلعرفتهم» is conjoined to it. «بسيماهم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «عرفتهم».
(وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِي لَحْنِ الْقَوْلِ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَعْمالَكُمْ) The «واو» is a conjunction; the lām with the nūn falls in the response to an omitted oath. «تعرفنهم» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you", and the «هاء» is a mafʿūl bihi. «في لحن القول» is attached to «تعرفنهم», or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while they are speaking allusively". «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يعلم أعمالكم» is the khabar; the clause is resumptive.
(وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ حَتَّى نَعْلَمَ الْمُجاهِدِينَ مِنْكُمْ وَالصَّابِرِينَ وَنَبْلُوَا أَخْبارَكُمْ) The lām falls in the response to an omitted oath, with the nūn. «نبلونكم» is a verb, a latent fāʿil and an object. «حتى» is a particle of limit and genitive, or of purpose and genitive. «نعلم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after «حتى». «المجاهدين» is a mafʿūl bihi and «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «الصابرين» is conjoined to «المجاهدين». «نبلو» is conjoined to «نعلم», and «أخباركم» is a mafʿūl bihi.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَشَاقُّوا الرَّسُولَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْهُدى لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئاً وَسَيُحْبِطُ أَعْمالَهُمْ) «إن» and its ism; the clause «كفروا» is a ṣila; the clause «صدوا عن سبيل الله» is conjoined to the clause «كفروا», and «شاقوا الرسول» is likewise conjoined. «من بعد» is attached to «شاقوا». «ما» is maṣdarī, and it with what it governs is in the interpretation of a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to «بعد». «لهم» is attached to «تبين» and «الهدى» is the fāʿil. «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and future. «يضروا الله» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «لن», and the clause is the khabar of «إن». «شيئا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "any harm"; you may also analyse it as a mafʿūl bihi. «وسيحبط»: the «واو» is a conjunction, the «سين» a particle of the future, and «يحبط أعمالهم» is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَلا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمالَكُمْ) The i'rab of the like of this verse has been given many times. The disagreement between the Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila has become intense over the major sins and whether good deeds are nullified; let whoever wishes return to that in the various places where it is treated.

dervis-irab:34-38.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّلْمِ) With fatḥa or kasra on the sīn: reconciliation, peace. It has been read with both.
(يَتِرَكُمْ) "Diminish you", from «وترتُ الرجل» when you have killed one of his, a son, a brother or a close relative; from «الوتر», which is being left alone. In al-Mukhtār: "«ووتره حقَّه يتِره» (with kasra) «وَتْرًا» (also with kasra [as read]) means he diminished him. His saying, Exalted is He: «ولن يتركم أعمالكم» means 'in your deeds', like their saying «دخلت البيت», i.e. 'into the house'. «أوتره» means he made him single, and from it «أوتر صلاته» ('he made his prayer odd-numbered') and «أوتر فرسه وتّرها توتيرا» are of one meaning." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "One says «وترتُ العدد وَتْرًا» (of the pattern waʿada) meaning I made it single, and «أوترته» with alif is the same; «وترتُ الصلاة وأوترتها» means I made it odd-numbered; and «وترتُ زيدًا حقَّه» (also of the pattern waʿada) means I diminished him in his right. From it: 'Whoever misses the ʿAṣr prayer, it is as if he has been robbed («وُتِر») of his family and his property'", with its nouns in the accusative as objects.
(فَيُحْفِكُمْ) He presses hard in asking for it until he takes it all, thereby distressing you. «الإحفاء» is exaggeration and reaching the limit in everything. One says «أحفى شاربه» when he removed it entirely. In al-Qāmūs: "«وحفا شاربه» means he was extreme in trimming it, like «أحفاه»."

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) «إن» and its ism; the clause «كفروا» is a ṣila (relative clause); «صدوا» is conjoined to «كفروا»; «عن سبيل الله» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «صدوا».
(ثُمَّ ماتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ) «ثم» is a conjunction; «ماتوا» is a verb and fāʿil (agent). The clause «فلن يغفر الله لهم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the «فاء» entered because of the sense of condition in the relative noun.
(فَلا تَهِنُوا وَتَدْعُوا إِلَى السَّلْمِ وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ) The «فاء» is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "when you have come to know the obligation of jihad, do not weaken and do not falter". «لا» is prohibitive; «تهنوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لا», and the «واو» is the fāʿil. «تدعوا» is conjoined to «فلا تهنوا», jussive likewise. «إلى السلم» is attached to «تدعوا». The «واو» is for ḥāl (circumstantial); «وأنتم الأعلون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is circumstantial.
(وَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ وَلَنْ يَتِرَكُمْ أَعْمالَكُمْ) The «واو» is also for ḥāl. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, and «معكم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar. The «واو» is a conjunction; «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and future; «يتركم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «لن»; «أعمالكم» is accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), as the author of al-Mukhtār stated, and the implication of the words of the author of al-Miṣbāḥ is that it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(إِنَّمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ) «إنما» is a restraining particle together with the thing it restrains (kāffa and makfūfa). «الحياة الدنيا» is a mubtadaʾ, «لعب» is the khabar, and «لهو» is conjoined to «لعب».
(وَإِنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا يُؤْتِكُمْ أُجُورَكُمْ وَلا يَسْئَلْكُمْ أَمْوالَكُمْ) The «واو» is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «تؤمنوا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive by the omission of the nūn, and the «واو» is the fāʿil; «تتقوا» is conjoined to «تؤمنوا». «يؤتكم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the «كاف» being the first object of «يؤتكم» and «أجوركم» the second. The «واو» is a conjunction; «لا» is negative; «يسألكم» is conjoined to «يؤتكم»; the «كاف» is the first object of «يسأل» and «أموالكم» its second, i.e. He does not command you to give out all your wealth in zakāt, but commands the giving of what is made obligatory upon you in zakāt, which is well known and set out at length in the books of jurisprudence.
(إِنْ يَسْئَلْكُمُوها فَيُحْفِكُمْ تَبْخَلُوا وَيُخْرِجْ أَضْغانَكُمْ) «إن» is conditional; «يسألكموها» is the protasis, jussive; the «كاف» is its first object and the «هاء» its second; the «ميم» is the sign of the masculine plural and the «واو» is for prolongation. «فيحفكم» is conjoined to the protasis. «تبخلوا» is the apodosis. «ويخرج» is conjoined to the apodosis and «أضغانكم» is a mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil refers back to Allah, Exalted is He, "because you are a people who love wealth, and one who is contested over what he loves, his hidden feelings that he conceals come to light".
(ها أَنْتُمْ هؤُلاءِ تُدْعَوْنَ لِتُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) «ها أنتم هؤلاء»: the like of this was discussed fully earlier, and we repeat some of what was said. «ها» is for attention, «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ and «هؤلاء» its khabar, and the clause «تدعون» is resumptive. Some analysed it as: «ها» for attention, «أنتم» a mubtadaʾ, the clause «تدعون» its khabar, and «هؤلاء» a vocative parenthetically placed between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to analysing «هؤلاء» as a relative noun meaning «الذين», being the khabar, with the clause «تدعون» as a ṣila, and al-Bayḍāwī followed him; «ها» of attention was repeated for emphasis. Abu Hayyān said: "«هؤلاء» is a relative noun when preceded by interrogative «ما» by agreement, or by interrogative «من» with disagreement"; the Kufans do not stipulate that, and al-Zamakhsharī followed their school. «لتنفقوا»: the lām is for purpose, and «تنفقوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of purpose, with the «واو» as fāʿil. «في سبيل الله» is attached to «تنفقوا».
(فَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يَبْخَلُ، وَمَنْ يَبْخَلْ فَإِنَّما يَبْخَلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ) The «فاء» is a conjunction of derivation (tafrīʿ). «منكم» is a fronted khabar and «من» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «يبخل» is a ṣila. A clause must be implied for the derivation to be complete, i.e. "and among you is one who is generous"; this counterpart was omitted only because the setting is one of proof of miserliness. The «واو» is a conjunction; «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «يبخل» is the protasis; the «فاء» is a linking particle; «إنما» is a restraining particle with the thing it restrains; and the clause «فإنما» and what follows it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. «يبخل» is an imperfect verb, nominative. «عن نفسه» is attached to «يبخل», because it is made transitive by «على» and by «عن», by including the sense of withholding and transitivity; one says «بخلتُ عليه وعنه», and likewise «ضننتُ عليه وعنه».
(وَاللَّهُ الْغَنِيُّ وَأَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ) The «واو» is resumptive. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «الغني» its khabar; «وأنتم الفقراء» is conjoined to «والله الغني».
(وَإِنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أَمْثالَكُمْ) The «واو» is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause. «إن» is conditional; «تتولوا» is the protasis, and the «واو» is the fāʿil; «يستبدل» is the apodosis; «قوما» is a mafʿūl bihi and «غيركم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوما». «ثم» is a particle and «لا» is negative; «يكونوا» is conjoined to the apodosis, jussive, and the «واو» is the ism of «يكون» and «أمثالكم» is its khabar.
